newsitem.title: CROATIA: US grants $650,000 for Bosnia-Croatia rail repairs.
newsitem.headline: US grants $650,000 for Bosnia-Croatia rail repairs.

text.p: Croatian state railways (HZ) and the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) signed an agreement on Tuesday for a $1.5 million project to rebuild a railway line linking eastern Croatia and northern Bosnia.
State news agency HINA said the project would boost trade between Croatia and Bosnia and strengthen Bosnian traffic links with the rest of Europe.

The U.S. government will provide $400,000 for rebuilding a railway bridge and will pay another $250,000 for repairs to the track near Vinkovci, Ross Wherry, USAID General Development Manager for Croatia, told Reuters.
Wherry said the Croatian side committed itself to remove landmines along the tracks and to provide labour and some building materials, estimating its costs at some $980,000.

Hina quoted U.S. ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith as saying: "I hope Bosnia will soon ship coal and bauxite along this route to the Croatian (river) ports of Osijek and Vukovar and then to other European markets."
On Sunday U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright presided over a ceremony at the reopening of an important bridge across the Sava river linking Bosnia with Croatia.
The northern Bosnian border, which straddles its autonomous Serb republic, has been closed or severely restricted since Croatia broke away from Serbian-led federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
Bosnian officials earlier said they expected Croatia to agree this month to reopening several other border crossings along the river.
The railway track should be rebuilt by September 1997, HZ director Marijan Klaric told Hina.
